external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: A developer who pushes branches and may manually start a rebuild of main.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
external_entities.notes: The text refers to developers collectively; their location and trust zone are not stated.

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry reached during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
external_entities.notes: The registry is external to the system and is on the internet.

processes.name: git server
processes.description: The self-hosted git server receiving developer branches and providing source to the build runner.
processes.source_excerpt: our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network
processes.notes: Nobody has documented whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: The runner that fetches source, resolves dependencies, produces container images, pushes images, calls the deploy controller, and can be manually used by developers to rebuild main.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: The shared build token used to call the deploy controller is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up. The runner does not verify signatures on downloaded dependencies.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: The controller that accepts the current image release request and answers store-server release queries.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network
processes.notes: It holds one record identifying which image SHA the estate should be on.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small server in each store back office that asks for the current release, pulls images, and restarts the container when needed.
processes.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
processes.notes: There are about 1,200 store instances. Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the registry or to the controller.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: The till software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container
processes.notes: There are about 1,200 store instances running on store servers.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: The registry holding finished container images tagged with commit SHAs.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores. The registry allows store-server pulls.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: A developer pushes a branch to the self-hosted git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source from the git server after a merge to main starts a build.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches out to the public package registry to resolve dependencies using the lockfile.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.
data_flows.data_description: dependency packages resolved from the lockfile

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry; the image is tagged with the commit SHA.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.data_description: finished container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: set release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release
data_flows.notes: The runner authenticates with a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.
data_flows.data_description: current release request containing an image SHA

data_flows.name: start rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually kicks off a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

data_flows.name: query release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller for the current release once a minute.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current container image from the image registry when its running image differs from the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it pulls that image from the registry and restarts the container
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network containing the self-hosted git server and deploy controller.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The separate environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The estate of about 1,200 stores containing the store servers and till software.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: The internet location of the public package registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet
